newsitem.title: India: Bombay stocks seen buoyant, to test higher levels.
newsitem.headline: Bombay stocks seen buoyant, to test higher levels.

text.p: ** (0400 GMT) - Bombay stocks likely to continue their
strong rally on increased foreign fund buying and
** Market due for a technical correction after jumping four
percent this week, but mood remains buoyant --traders
** Bombay's top share index ends Tuesday 44.77 points, or
** Market seen unaffected by National Stock Exchange
move to declare five brokers in default and suspend six
others Tuesday for not honouring their commitments
Bombay shares are expected to open higher Wednesday, as more participants join the blistering foreign-funds led rally that has propelled the benchmark index to 20-month highs, traders said.
Chances of a market correction was lurking, but players said any reaction would attract fresh buying.
"A correction could come any time and even if it comes, it is not worrisome," said the head of dealing at a foreign brokerage.
"People have to get used to these high prices."

A sizzling 38 percent rally in the first half of 1997, largely led by foreign fund buying on attractive valuations, has made Indian stock exchanges the best performing Asian market this year, traders said.

They said local markets are likely to be largely unaffected by the National Stock Exchange move late Tuesday to declare five brokers in default and suspend six others for not honouring their commitments.
